Epidemiology

Epidemiology — health and disease in populations, the epidemiology chain, disease prevention, surveillance and investigation of outbreaks.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define epidemiology and its uses
  • Describe the chain of infection and ways to break it
  • Differentiate incidence and prevalence
  • List the steps of an outbreak investigation

In simple words

Epidemiology is the study of how disease spreads and how often it occurs in groups of people. It answers: who is sick, where, when and why — and that guides control action.

Common terms

Term Meaning
Incidence Number of new cases in a period
Prevalence Number of all cases at a time
Endemic Constantly present in a place
Epidemic Sudden increase above expected level
Pandemic Epidemic in many countries
Sporadic Scattered, occasional cases
Case fatality rate Deaths among cases
Portal of entry How the agent enters a new host

Chain of infection

  1. Infectious agent — bacteria, virus, fungus, parasite
  2. Reservoir / source — person, animal, soil, water
  3. Portal of exit — respiratory, faeco-oral, blood, skin
  4. Mode of transmission — contact, droplet, vehicle, vector
  5. Portal of entry — same ways into the new host
  6. Susceptible host — immunity, age, nutrition, illness

Nursing breaks the chain by handwashing, isolation, immunisation, safe water, food hygiene, vector control and nurse’s treatment of cases.

Steps of outbreak investigation

  1. Verify the facts and confirm the diagnosis
  2. Define and count cases (person, place, time)
  3. Draw the epidemic curve and map
  4. Form a hypothesis about source and route
  5. Control: isolate, treat, protect contacts, remove the source
  6. Report to health authorities and communicate with the community
  7. Follow up and evaluate control measures

🔴 Break the chain anywhere and stop the disease

You do not need to remove every link. Handwashing, immunisation, safe water and one reported case can stop an outbreak — that is why nursing action is so valuable.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Epidemiology studies disease in populations and its spread.
  2. Incidence = new cases; prevalence = all cases at a time.
  3. Endemic = constant; epidemic = sudden excess; pandemic = over countries.
  4. Chain: agent, reservoir, portal of exit, transmission, portal of entry, host.
  5. Outbreak steps: verify, define, control, report, follow up.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Case fatality rate is the proportion of cases who die.
  2. Attack rate = cases among those exposed.
  3. Handwashing is the single most important nursing intervention to break transmission.
  4. Epidemic curve shows the speed and spread of an outbreak.
  5. Notify diseases such as cholera, plague and diphtheria immediately.

📌 Memory trick

Chain of infection: A-R-P-P-P-S — Agent, Reservoir, Portal (exit and entry), Path, Susceptible host.

60-second revision

  • Epidemiology: who, where, when and why of disease.
  • Incidence new cases; prevalence all cases.
  • Sporadic, endemic, epidemic, pandemic.
  • Chain: agent, reservoir, portals, transmission, host.
  • Outbreak steps: verify, define, control, report, follow up.

Test yourself

Prevalence counts:

Answer: B. Prevalence is the number of existing cases at a given time, new and old.

An epidemic in many countries is called a:

Answer: B. A pandemic is an epidemic occurring in several countries or continents.

Which is a mode of transmission?

Answer: C. Transmission modes include contact, droplet, vehicle-borne, airborne and vector-borne.

Which nursing action best breaks the chain of infection?

Answer: B. Hand hygiene interrupts transmission at multiple points and is the single most effective routine measure.

The first step in an outbreak investigation is to:

Answer: B. The first step is verification of the diagnosis and confirmation that an outbreak exists.
